question: to the Commission Barbara Bonte (PfE) Subject:
GSP status of Cuba in light of the systematic torture of 1 260 political prisoners

Cuba enjoys preferential market access to the European Union under the Generalised Scheme of Preferences (GSP). However, the Prisoners Defenders report describes how the Cuban regime abuses and mistreats thousands of political prisoners, including through prolonged solitary confinement, sleep deprivation, forced postures, physical abuse and the systematic denial of medical care. Of the 1 260 political prisoners, 128 are women and 32 were arrested as minors. 1.

Is the Commission aware of the report by Prisoners Defenders documenting a record high of 1 260 political prisoners in Cuba, as well as systematic torture, sexual violence and death threats as routine practices of the regime?
Does the Commission agree that the torture and ill-treatment of political prisoners, of which there are more and more, is a violation of the conditions laid down in the GSP scheme?

Is the Commission considering opening a formal investigation procedure that could lead to the temporary suspension of Cuba from the GSP scheme, in accordance with Article 19 of Regulation (EU) No 978/2012, as long as the regime continues to torture its political prisoners and uses them as forced labourers for the production of export goods destined for the EU?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (3.8.2026) The Commission is aware of the report by Prisoner Defenders to which reference is made in the question. As recalled the intervention1 of High Representative/Vice-President of the Commission at the plenary of the European Parliament on 19 May 2026, Cuba urgently needs to make fundamental political, economic and democratic reforms, respecting the human rights and fundamental freedoms of the Cuban people and releasing political prisoners and all individuals who have been arbitrarily detained. The EU including through its Delegation in Havana and its Special Representative for Human Rights regularly raises individual cases of political prisoners with the Cuban authorities calling for their immediate release. The EU has regularly called the Cuban authorities to ensure that all persons deprived of their liberty are treated in full compliance with international human rights standards. Cuba is not a beneficiary of the EU generalised scheme of preferences nor of any EU preferential trade regime, hence the premise underlying questions 2 and 3 does not apply.
